correctness.rationale: Exact projector algebra gives sym((I-2P)(I-2P0))=I-2(P-P0)^2. The split-energy gradient has the form (I-2P0)grad F; for delta<1/sqrt(2), dF/dt<=-beta(1-2delta^2)||grad F||^2. Strong convexity yields the global gradient-dominance inequality and exponential energy decay, while coercivity prevents escape. A planar quadratic with a projector rotated by phi has the exact scaled rotation ODE and radius exp(-beta mu cos(2phi)t), proving the rate optimal, pure rotation at phi=pi/4, and exponential instability beyond. The k-dimensional embedding is explicit. The exact rational checker reproduces five finite projector identities and critical/off-critical examples; no finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The literature establishes continuous-time perturbed HiSD local sufficient stability under mu-2 alpha L>0 (Shi et al., Theorem 3) and a 45-degree instantaneous gradient/ascent-subspace criterion (Chu and Lin, Section 2), but not the fixed-eigenspace, nonlinear all-start, arbitrary time-varying projector tolerance with sharp energy exponent and periodic critical counterexample. Huang et al. give a different local/discrete inexact-frame bound. Actual searches of published mathematical records identified no implication covering this conjunction. The 45-degree trigonometry and projector identity themselves are standard, not claimed as new; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Classical sectorial-gradient, robust differential-inclusion, or accretive-operator results could imply the energy-decay argument with a generic cosine condition; an independent historical priority audit is needed.

The analysis is deliberately restricted to fixed, uncoupled stable/unstable eigenspaces; rotating eigenspaces may invalidate the Lyapunov transform.

value.rationale: Accurate unstable eigenspaces are the bottleneck of high-index saddle search; source perturbation criteria deteriorate with spectral conditioning and only guarantee local convergence. On a mathematically natural separable strongly concave-convex class, a sharp 45-degree error cone yields condition-number-independent global convergence from all initial states under arbitrary time-varying subspace perturbations, a sharp rate attained even at equal curvature, and a critical family of periodic orbits showing exact failure. The threshold is motivated by the published subspace-error gap and the critical dynamics, not an arbitrary parameter slice. No assertion of priority for basic projector algebra is made.
